statement: The Owner MUST be able to open the settings file in the editor, it being written first with an empty editor command when it is missing.

title: The chat listens only in front, and only when asked
statement: Voice activation MUST be off until the Owner turns it on, and the chat MUST listen only while its window is in front: going behind another window or app stops listening and leaves the draft.

title: Quick mode sends when the Owner has finished
statement: With Quick mode on, a dictated message MUST be sent by itself after a pause judged on the Mac from the words and the voice's pitch: about half a second after a finished thought, 3 to 4 seconds mid-thought and about 2 seconds when unsure; a countdown MUST show on Send, and any sound or key MUST cancel it.

title: The sign-in is given its code
statement: The Owner MUST be able to give the sign-in under way the code the browser showed.

title: A sign-in under way can be canceled
statement: The Owner MUST be able to cancel a sign-in under way, leaving the agent as it was.

title: The Owner signs the agent out
statement: The Owner MUST be able to sign the agent out from inside the product, so another account can sign in, and signing out MUST be refused while a sign-in runs.

title: A product kind gets a table of its own
statement: A product kind MUST give the product a table named after the kind, with an ID, a title, a required reference to its parent kind and a stored field for each of its fields, typed and required as declared; an obligation kind MUST join the obligation supertype.

title: A product kind keeps its own label, stage and obligation
statement: A product kind MUST be listed after Lathe's kinds, with its own label, stage and obligation, in any of the six stages or none, and MUST NOT change any of Lathe's kinds.

title: A kind declared twice is refused, naming its file and line
statement: Two product kinds with the same name MUST be refused by the store, naming the file and line of the second and the line of the first.

title: A product relation declared twice is refused, naming the file and line
statement: The store MUST refuse a product relation with the same name, source kind and target kind as another, once, naming its file and line.

title: The product's own kinds are read whole first
statement: Before declaring more, the Owner MUST be able to read the product whole, with each kind of its own, that kind's fields, and its relations.

title: What the reference would leave blank is refused
statement: The store MUST refuse a product kind or relation without a description, and a check without its summary or explanation; Lathe's own tables, kinds and checks MUST all be described.

title: A product places its own kinds in a stage
statement: A product kind MAY name one of the six stages, or none, and MUST NOT add a stage or change one of Lathe's kinds.

title: A product is added with its roles
statement: Adding a product MUST add it with its title, its description and its roles, the root every record of its specification sits under.

title: A product that breaks its rules is refused
statement: An added product that breaks a rule of the Product aggregate, such as an ID already taken, MUST be refused, giving every reason and changing nothing.

title: A product kind changes in place
statement: A product kind's label, description, parent kind, stage, obligation, ID pattern, example or title form, or its fields (the whole list, in order), MUST change as given, and the next load MUST read the product's records of the kind by the changed kind.

title: A change a record of the kind no longer fits is refused
statement: A change to a product kind that a record of the kind no longer fits MUST be refused, giving every reason and changing nothing.

title: A product kind is removed with its fields
statement: Removing a product kind MUST remove its declaration with its fields, and the next load MUST read the product without the kind.

title: A kind the product still uses is refused
statement: Removing a product kind MUST be refused, giving every reason and changing nothing, while the product has records of the kind or a relation or another kind names it.

title: A product relation's role, labels and description change
statement: A product relation pair's role, labels and description MUST change as given; its name and its kinds are its key and MUST stay.

title: A change that breaks the relation's rules is refused
statement: A change to a product relation that breaks a rule of the Product aggregate MUST be refused, giving every reason and changing nothing.

title: A product relation pair is removed
statement: Removing a product relation pair MUST remove the pair and leave the product's other relations as they were.

title: A pair that still has a link is refused
statement: Removing a product relation pair MUST be refused, giving every reason and changing nothing, while a link of the pair is left.

title: An open question changes in place
statement: An open question's title, owner and description MUST change as given, and the records it is about MUST be replaced as a list; its product or domain MUST change only by moving it.

title: A question that breaks its rules is refused
statement: A change to an open question that breaks a rule of the Product aggregate, such as an owner that is no role of the product, MUST be refused, giving every reason and changing nothing.

title: An interface is removed with its roles and what it offers
statement: Removing an interface MUST remove it with its roles and the links to the use cases it offers, never the use cases.

title: An interface something names is refused
statement: Removing an interface MUST be refused, giving every reason and changing nothing, while a variant step or a view names it, or anything else references it.

title: A business outcome is removed with its measures
statement: Removing a business outcome MUST remove it with the links to the records that measure it, never the records.

title: An outcome an aggregate, read model or journey serves is refused
statement: Removing a business outcome MUST be refused, giving every reason and changing nothing, while an aggregate, a read model or a journey serves it or anything else references it.

title: A journey changes in place
statement: A journey's title, trigger, result and notes MUST change as given, and the business outcomes it serves MUST be replaced as a list; its product MUST stay.

title: A journey that breaks its rules is refused
statement: A change to a journey that breaks a rule of the Journey aggregate, such as an outcome that is not its own product's, MUST be refused, giving every reason and changing nothing.

title: The reference script prints the reference, or writes it to a file
statement: The reference MUST be written as Markdown: how data is kept, then the kinds with their tables, the other tables, the relations, the stages and the checks, each with its own anchor. The Owner MUST be able to print it or write it to a file of their choosing.

title: The reference gives every fact of each kind, table, relation, stage and check
statement: The reference MUST give each kind's label, description, stage, parents and children, obligation (yes or no), ID pattern and ID scope; each table's role, keys and fields with their types, values, references and descriptions; each relation's role, labels, description and pairs; each stage's position, label and description; and each check's name, severity, summary, explanation and kinds. The engine's own problem, `data-refused`, MUST be listed as a check too, and the reference MUST say that clean architecture's use case is a command handler in Lathe.

title: A product's reference shows its own kinds and its own checks
statement: The reference MUST be the product's own: its kinds, tables and relations with its declarations, and its own checks after Lathe's and the engine's.

title: Lathe's committed reference never goes stale
statement: Lathe's reference MUST be committed as `lathe/REFERENCE.md`, so an agent can read it without running anything. The package build MUST regenerate it, and a test MUST fail when the committed file differs from what the reference script writes. It is generated from the schema and the checks, never written by hand.

title: Relations read in plain words from both ends
statement: Each relation MUST carry a `forward_label`, the link read from its source ("Raises"), and a `reverse_label`, the link read from its target ("Raised by"), in sentence case. The reference MUST show both and list each kind's links out by their forward labels and its links in by their reverse labels. The store MUST refuse a product relation without both.

title: The engine loads the stages and each kind's stage and position
statement: The engine MUST load the stages in order and each kind's stage and position from the schema. The product and open questions MUST sit outside the stages.

title: Kinds are read in one order, the schema's
statement: Every list of kinds, in the app, the reference and coverage, MUST read them in one order: Lathe's kinds by their position in the schema (the product, then stage by stage, each kind by its position, then open questions), then a product's own kinds by name. No code MAY keep a list of its own.

title: A journey is removed whole
statement: Removing a journey MUST remove it with its steps, its journey test and the links they start, and MUST NOT remove the use cases and policies its steps carry out.

title: A journey something names is refused
statement: Removing a journey MUST be refused, giving every reason and changing nothing, while anything outside it references what is in it.

title: A journey step is removed with its link
statement: Removing a journey step MUST remove it with the link it starts, never the use case or policy it carried out.

title: A step something references is refused
statement: Removing a journey step MUST be refused, giving every reason and changing nothing, while anything else references it.

title: A journey test changes in place
statement: A journey test's way of running, steps and expected result MUST change as given, and the test data sets it starts from MUST be replaced as a list.

title: A test that breaks its rules is refused
statement: A change to a journey test that breaks a rule of the Journey aggregate, such as an automated test that names no file, MUST be refused, giving every reason and changing nothing.

title: A journey test is removed with its links
statement: Removing a journey test MUST remove it with the links it starts.

title: A test something references is refused
statement: Removing a journey test MUST be refused, giving every reason and changing nothing, while anything else references it, such as a business outcome it measures.

title: A kind or check met while reading opens its reference in one step
statement: Wherever the Reader meets a kind or a check while reading the spec (a record's kind, a problem's code, a field), they MUST be able to open what the reference says about it in one step, without leaving the workbench.

title: The Reader reads a journey step by step
statement: The Reader MUST be able to read a journey's steps in order on each path, the main path first, with what each carries out, who acts and where it sits, and see where the acting role changes.

title: A use case or policy names the journeys it is a step of
statement: A use case's and a policy's page MUST name each journey it is a step of, with the step, its path and position and the steps before and after it, each a link.

title: In the graph a journey's steps sit under it in order
statement: In the graph a journey's steps MUST sit under it, in order on each path, each linked to what it carries out.

title: A business outcome sits under its product and is measurable
statement: A business outcome MUST sit under its product and give a statement of the outcome, its measure and its target; the store MUST refuse one that leaves any of them out.

title: Discovery is the first stage, holding outcomes and journeys
statement: Discovery MUST be the first stage, before the domain model, and hold the business outcomes and the journeys that reach them, which follow the product in the kinds' order.

title: A business outcome is found and read whole
statement: The Owner MUST be able to list a product's business outcomes and read one whole, with what serves it and what measures it, before changing it.

title: A product's interfaces each have a kind, roles and use cases
statement: Each interface of a product MUST have one kind (web, desktop, API, command line, agent tools or other), the roles of the product that use it and the use cases it offers, and MUST go with its roles and offers, refused while referenced.

title: The product is read whole with its interfaces
statement: The Owner MUST be able to read the product whole, with its interfaces, before changing them.

title: A journey runs from a trigger to a result, under its product
statement: A journey MUST sit under its product and give its trigger, what starts it in the world, and its result, what it ends in; the store MUST refuse one that leaves either out.

title: A journey serves outcomes beside the aggregates and read models
statement: A journey MAY serve any number of its product's business outcomes, each a serves link from the journey, beside the aggregates and read models that serve them; the use cases and policies its steps carry out MUST then serve those outcomes through it.

title: A journey of fewer than two use cases is warned
statement: A journey whose steps carry out fewer than two use cases MUST be warned of as a use case, not a journey.

title: A handoff its previous use case does not lead to is warned
statement: A handoff step whose policy hears no event raised by the result of the use case step before it MUST be warned of, once that use case has a flow.

title: An outcome timing a duration that no journey serves is warned
statement: A business outcome whose measure reads as a duration, such as the days from one thing to another, MUST be warned of while no journey serves it, saying to write the journey it times.

title: A journey is read whole first
statement: The Owner MUST be able to read a journey whole, its steps path by path with what each carries out, before changing it.

title: A record of a product's own kind is held to its declaration
statement: A record of a product's own kind MUST be added, changed and removed only through the Extension record's commands, each held to its kind's declared fields and relations, and MUST go with its links and packages, refused while anything references it.

title: A record of the product's own kind is found and read whole
statement: The Owner MUST be able to list a parent's records of one of the product's own kinds and read one whole, with its fields and links, before changing it.

title: A product names the roles its use cases name
statement: A product MUST list the roles its use cases and interfaces name, each with a description of the part it plays.

title: The product is read whole with its roles
statement: The Owner MUST be able to read the product whole, with its roles, before changing them.

title: An open question sits where it is asked
statement: An open question MUST sit under its product or one of its domains and MAY be about any records of its product; a decided question is removed with its links, its answer written into the records it affects.

title: Open questions are read with what each is about
statement: The Owner MUST be able to read the product whole, with its open questions and the records each is about.

title: A product relation adds a link table or a pair
statement: A product_relation with a new name MUST get a link table of its own; one with Lathe's name MUST add only its pair, and MUST change nothing else of that relation.

title: A product's own interface design kind presents commands and queries, as a view does
statement: A product MAY let a kind of its own whose stage is interface design present commands and queries, by a product relation named presents from that kind to command or to query, so one record (an invocation) presents several commands and queries of any of the product's domains, as a view does; a product relation named presents from any other kind MUST be refused.

title: Tests and the product's own records measure outcomes
statement: A business outcome MAY be measured by any number of tests of any kind, each a measured_by link from the outcome, and a test MAY measure several outcomes. A record of a product's own kind (a report, a script, a check) MAY measure one only once the product allows that kind with a product_relation named measured_by; no other kind of Lathe's measures. An outcome that nothing in the code can measure MAY say instead how it is measured outside the code.

title: Change an interface refuses what breaks a rule
statement: Changes an interface's title, kind, description, whether it is public, the roles that use it or the use cases it offers (each list replaced whole). It MUST be refused with every reason when what it is given breaks a rule, and leave every data file as it was.

title: A step carries out a use case or a handoff of its product
statement: Each step of a journey MAY carry out one use case of any domain of the journey's product, or one of its policies as a handoff, and MUST carry out nothing of another product; a step that carries out nothing yet MUST be allowed, and is reported as a use case still to write.

title: A journey's steps are in order on each path
statement: A journey's steps MUST be in order on its main path and on each alternate path, every path numbered 1, 2, 3 without gaps, and moving a step MUST keep every path so numbered.

title: Move a journey step refuses what breaks a rule
statement: Moves a step to another position, on its own path or another, shifting the steps of the old path and the new so each stays numbered 1, 2, 3. It MUST be refused with every reason when what it is given breaks a rule, and leave every data file as it was.

title: Change a journey step refuses what breaks a rule
statement: Changes a step's title, or the use case or policy it carries out (null clears it). It MUST be refused with every reason when what it is given breaks a rule, and leave every data file as it was.

title: A journey has at most one journey test
statement: A journey MAY have one journey test, which drives its main path end to end from its trigger to its result at the service, system or browser level, and MUST NOT have two.

title: Change an extension record refuses what breaks a rule
statement: Changes a record of a product's own kind: its title or declared fields, the links it starts by relation, the packages it uses or its helper files. It MUST be refused with every reason when what it is given breaks a rule, and leave every data file as it was.

title: Remove an extension record refuses what breaks a rule
statement: Removes a record of a product's own kind with the links it starts, the packages it uses and its helper files. It MUST be refused with every reason when what it is given breaks a rule, and leave every data file as it was.

title: A record of the product's own kind moves to another domain
statement: The Owner MUST be able to move a record of the product's own kind that sits in a domain to another domain of its product, where it takes that domain's ID.

title: Move an open question refuses what breaks a rule
statement: Moves an open question under its product or another of its domains. It MUST be refused with every reason when what it is given breaks a rule, and leave every data file as it was.

title: Remove an open question refuses what breaks a rule
statement: Removes an open question with what it is about, once it is decided and its answer is written into the records it affects. It MUST be refused with every reason when what it is given breaks a rule, and leave every data file as it was.

title: An entry point is removed whole
statement: Removing an entry point MUST remove it with the packages and helper files it names and the links it starts.

title: An entry point something references is refused
statement: Removing an entry point MUST be refused, giving every reason and changing nothing, while anything references it.

title: A tooling record is removed whole
statement: Removing a tooling record MUST remove it with the packages and helper files it names and the links it starts.

title: A tooling record something references is refused
statement: Removing a tooling record MUST be refused, giving every reason and changing nothing, while anything references it.

title: A standard's title and description change
statement: A standard's title and description MUST change as given, and its product MUST never change.

title: A standard that breaks its rules is refused
statement: A change to a standard that breaks a rule of the Standard aggregate MUST be refused, giving every reason and changing nothing.

title: A standard is removed whole
statement: Removing a standard MUST remove it with its rules, their rule tests and the links they start.

title: A standard whose rule a record meets is refused
statement: Removing a standard MUST be refused, giving every reason and changing nothing, while anything outside it references what is in it, such as a technical record that meets a rule.

title: A rule is added to its standard
statement: Adding a standard rule MUST add it under its standard, with its title, its statement and the heading it is shown under.

title: A rule that breaks its rules is refused
statement: An added standard rule that breaks a rule of the Standard aggregate, such as an ID already taken, MUST be refused, giving every reason and changing nothing.

title: A standard rule is removed with its tests
statement: Removing a standard rule MUST remove it with its tests and the links they start.

title: A rule a record meets is refused
statement: Removing a standard rule MUST be refused, giving every reason and changing nothing, while a technical record meets it or anything else references it or its tests.

title: A standard rule test changes in place
statement: A standard rule test's way of running MUST change as given, and the test data sets it starts from MUST be replaced as a list.

title: A standard rule test that breaks its rules is refused
statement: A change to a standard rule test that breaks a rule of the Standard aggregate, such as an automated test that names no file, MUST be refused, giving every reason and changing nothing.

title: A standard rule test is removed
statement: Removing a standard rule test MUST remove it with the links it starts.

title: A standard rule test something references is refused
statement: Removing a standard rule test MUST be refused, giving every reason and changing nothing, while anything references it.

title: A table is removed whole
statement: Removing a table MUST remove it with its keys and the links, packages and helper files it names.

title: A table something references is refused
statement: Removing a table MUST be refused, giving every reason and changing nothing, while anything else references it, such as another table's foreign key.

title: Standards, their tests and meets are in the schema
statement:
The schema MUST have a `standard` kind under the product and a `standard_rule` kind under a standard, in the technical specification stage, with IDs `

-STD-` and `-R`; a `standard_rule_test` kind under a standard rule, in the test plan stage, with IDs `-T`, any number per rule, at any level; and the relation `meets` from a technical record to a standard rule, labeled Meets and Met by, with no role. The reference MUST describe them.

title: A standard is found and read whole
statement: The Owner MUST be able to list a product's standards and read one whole, with its rules and their tests, before changing it.

title: Each technical record sits under the record it builds and names its file
statement: Each technical record MUST sit under the record it builds, as its kind says: a data model and a table under an entity, a read model or its domain; a projection under a read model; a command handler under a command; a query handler under a query; an event handler under a policy; an event type under an event; a value type under a value object; a predicate under a specification; an endpoint handler under an endpoint; an adapter under an integration; a repository, a service and a UI component under their domain. It MAY name its file, relative to the repo root; a file that does not exist yet is work still to do.

title: A table stores only what fields can't say
statement: A table's stored fields MUST follow from its entity's or read model's fields, with value objects flattened; the table MUST store its name, its storage and its keys, and a unique key MAY name the invariant it enforces.

title: A record can point at the code that builds or proves it
statement: A technical record MUST be able to name its `file`, and a test its run by's `file` that runs it, each as a path relative to the repo root.

title: A table is found and read whole
statement: The Owner MUST be able to list the tables under an entity, read model or domain and read one whole, with its keys, before changing it.

title: An entry point names the file that starts it
statement: An entry point MUST sit under its domain, be titled by its identifier exactly as in code, and name the file that starts the product or one of its processes.

title: A domain's entry points are found and read
statement: The Owner MUST be able to list a domain's entry points and read each, with the packages it uses and the rules it meets, before changing them.

title: Tooling names its script or configuration
statement: A tooling record MUST sit under its domain, be titled by its identifier exactly as in code, and name the script or configuration file that builds, checks or tests the product.

title: A tooling record is found and read whole
statement: The Owner MUST be able to list a domain's tooling records and read one whole, with the packages it uses, the rules it meets and what it generates, before changing it.

title: Every repository, reader and table names its one data store
statement: The schema MUST have `data_store`, under a product or one of its domains, with its kind, and the relations `stored_in` (each repository, reader or table to at most one data store) and `provided_by` (a data store to at most one integration); coverage MUST report a repository, reader or table that names no data store, and a data store nothing is kept in.

title: A data store is found and read whole
statement: The Owner MUST be able to list a product's or domain's data stores and read one whole, with what is kept there and what provides it, before changing it.

title: A standard rule is owed, met by technical records and proved by its tests
statement: A standard rule MUST be an obligation of the product: designed and built by the technical records that meet it, and proved by its standard rule tests, automated or manual, whose file names them. One that nothing meets MUST be reported as not designed, and one with no such test as not proved.

title: Change a standard rule refuses what breaks a rule
statement: Changes a standard rule's title, statement or group. It MUST be refused with every reason when what it is given breaks a rule, and leave every data file as it was.

title: Change a table refuses what breaks a rule
statement: Changes a table's title, name, storage or file, its keys (the whole list, in order), the data store it is kept in (null clears it), or the standard rules it meets, the packages it uses or its helper files (each the whole list). It MUST be refused with every reason when what it is given breaks a rule, and leave every data file as it was.

title: Move a table refuses what breaks a rule
statement: Moves a table, with its keys, under another entity, read model or domain: exactly one is given, and it replaces the parent it had. It MUST be refused with every reason when what it is given breaks a rule, and leave every data file as it was.

title: Change an entry point refuses what breaks a rule
statement: Changes an entry point's title, file, description, packages, helper files or standard rules met. It MUST be refused with every reason when what it is given breaks a rule, and leave every data file as it was.

title: An entry point moves to another domain
statement: The Owner MUST be able to move an entry point to another domain of its product, where it takes that domain's ID.

title: Change a tooling record refuses what breaks a rule
statement: Changes a tooling record's title, file, packages, helper files, standard rules met or technical records generated. It MUST be refused with every reason when what it is given breaks a rule, and leave every data file as it was.

title: A tooling record moves to another domain
statement: The Owner MUST be able to move a tooling record to another domain of its product, where it takes that domain's ID.

title: A data store changes, and goes only when nothing is kept in it
statement: The Owner MUST be able to change a data store's kind or description, and remove one only while nothing is kept in it.

title: Remove a data store refuses what breaks a rule
statement: Removes a data store whole. It MUST be refused with every reason when what it is given breaks a rule, and leave every data file as it was.

title: A domain's data store moves to another domain
statement: The Owner MUST be able to move a data store of one domain to another domain of its product, where it takes that domain's ID.

title: Coverage counts designed and proved obligations
statement: For each domain, coverage MUST give the number of obligations of each obligation kind, and how many of each are designed and how many are proved. Built counts are LA-TRC-UC01-R04; not-automated-yet counts are LA-TRC-UC01-R09.

title: Coverage lists each gap with what it lacks
statement: Coverage MUST list each obligation that is not designed, not built or not proved, with its kind, saying which it lacks, and the `not-designed`, `not-built` and `not-proved` warnings MUST name exactly the obligations coverage counts as lacking it.

title: Coverage gaps are warnings, not errors
statement: A gap MUST be reported as a warning, so that an honest, unfinished design still passes `lathe check`.

title: Coverage reports built separately from designed
statement: For each domain, coverage MUST give how many obligations of each kind are built: every technical record that implements its design names a file that exists, and there is at least one. The built count MUST never be more than the designed count, so a domain whose code does not exist yet shows as designed but not built.

title: Coverage lists each record short of a minimum as a gap named by its rule
statement: Coverage MUST list, under the record's own scope, each record short of a minimum the schema leaves to coverage (an aggregate with no root, a use case with no flow, an entity with no storage of its own unless it is stored with its root, and the rest of the gap rules), as a gap named by its rule, never as a problem. Each gap rule MUST have a unique name, a stage and a one-sentence summary.

title: The Reader sees how complete each domain is and what is undecided or broken
statement: Opening a product, the Reader MUST see each domain with how much of it is designed, built and proved, and the product's open questions and problems, without running anything.

title: Coverage counts every obligation kind
statement: For each domain, coverage MUST give one entry per obligation kind (constraint, invariant, specification, policy, domain service, UC requirement, view requirement, API requirement, pattern rule, standard rule, and every product kind declared an obligation), in schema order, even when the domain has none of that kind. Each entry MUST give the total and how many are designed, built, proved and not automated yet.

title: Designed, built and proved follow from the tree
statement: An obligation MUST count as designed when its design is specified, as built when every one of the specific technical records that implement that design names a file that exists (and there is at least one), and as proved when a test under it is automated or manual, at a level its kind allows. A UC requirement is designed when a flow step of its use case fulfills it, and built when every record that carries out its fulfilling steps names a file that exists: the record that handles each command or query a step invokes, with the predicates of the specifications and the services of the domain services that command or query checks, selects by or calls, and the connector of each integration a step exchanges with (LA-TRC-UC01-R15); an interface part of the view a step happens in does not build it. Any other obligation is designed when the technical record of its kind exists, and built when every such record names a file that exists: a constraint's technical record (of its value object), an invariant's rule, a specification's predicate, a policy's event handling, a domain service's service, a view requirement's interface parts that build it, an API requirement's handling record (of its operation). A product relation declared with the design, build or proof role counts as design, build or proof of its target. Coverage is counted in the domain the obligation belongs to.

title: A test not automated yet makes an obligation not automated yet, not proved
statement: An obligation MUST count as proved only when an automated or manual test proves it, and as not automated yet when it is not proved but a test not automated yet is meant to prove it. The `not-proved` warning for such an obligation SHOULD say that its test is not automated yet.

title: The check prints one coverage line per domain and obligation kind
statement: `lathe check` MUST print one coverage line for each domain and obligation kind the domain has, with designed, built, proved and not-automated-yet counts out of the total and the number of gaps; a domain with no obligations gets one line saying so.

title: Each obligation kind says when it is built
statement: Coverage MUST count an obligation as built only through the specific code that builds it, by its kind, never through other code near it: an invariant when its rule names its file, a UC requirement when a step that fulfills it invokes a command or query whose handling record names its file, a view requirement when an interface part that builds it names its file (not one that only renders its view), an API requirement when the record that handles its operation names its file, a standard rule when a technical record that meets it names its file. A product's own obligation kind is built by the sources of the links its declaration gives the design or build role.

title: Proof counts only at a level the test's kind allows
statement: A test MUST count as proof only when its run by level is one its kind allows (LA-TRC-DS02); at another level it counts as nothing, and LA-CHK-UC01-R09 reports it.

title: A constraint counts in its value object's domain, or in Shared
statement: A constraint MUST count in the coverage of the domain its value object belongs to (`LA-PRD-UC37-R02`): the one domain whose entities, events or read models have fields typed by it. The constraint of a value object two or more domains use, or none, MUST count once, in the product's Shared coverage, and its one test proves it there.

title: A product proof that names a file is named in it
statement: A record of a product kind that a proof link names, and that names a file, MUST count as proof only when that file exists and names the record's ID, as a test's file must, and a record that names no file MUST count as it stands.

title: An integration's connector that carries out a step builds what the step fulfills
statement: A UC requirement MUST also count as built when a flow step that fulfills it exchanges with an integration whose connector names a file that exists: the connector carries the step out. A record of a product's own kind under that integration does not build it. This holds for every product.

title: An outcome nothing serves, and a use case group serving none, are gaps
statement: Coverage MUST report as gaps a business outcome no aggregate or read model serves, under the product outside every domain, and an aggregate or read model that a use case sits with and that serves no business outcome, under its domain; neither is a problem.

title: A source file no technical record names is a gap
statement: Coverage MUST report as a code-file-untraced gap, under the product outside every domain, each source file (the source patterns in the product's configuration, defaulting to code in the common languages) that no technical record names, directly or through a folder it names; tests (the test patterns and files in test folders), configurations, generated files and build output MUST be left out. Code MUST NOT need to carry record IDs for this.

title: An outcome nothing measures is a gap
statement: Coverage MUST report as a gap, under the product outside every domain, a business outcome that names no measure outside the code and that no record of a product's own kind and no test that runs measures: a test not automated yet, or an automated one whose file is missing or does not name it, measures nothing. It is never a problem.

title: A product's relation with a role counts on Lathe's obligation kinds too
statement: A relation a product declares with a role MUST count toward coverage for every obligation it links to, Lathe's own kinds included: a design link designs the obligation, a build link builds it when its source names a file that exists, and a proof link proves it as the product's own obligation kinds are proved; a design link on one of Lathe's kinds MUST NOT build it, since the kind says what builds it.

title: An integration's connector builds a policy that exchanges with it
statement: A policy that exchanges with an integration MUST count as built only when the code that carries the policy out and that integration's connector each name a file that exists: the connector carries out the policy's exchange. This holds for every product.

title: An automated test's file names the test's ID
statement: An automated test's `file` MUST name the test's own ID, matched only as a whole ID (LA-TRC-DS01). Otherwise the engine MUST report a `test-file-missing-id` error naming the test and the file, and the test MUST NOT count as proof.

title: A manual or not-yet-automated test's file is checked only for existing
statement: The engine MUST NOT report `test-file-missing-id` for a manual test or a test not automated yet; a file it names is checked only for existing.

title: A product proof's file is checked as a test's
statement: A record of a product kind that a proof link names, and that names a file, MUST be checked as an automated test is: the engine MUST report a test-file-missing error when the file does not exist, and a test-file-missing-id error when it does not name the record's ID. A record of a product kind that names a file but proves nothing MUST NOT be reported by either check.

title: Every test case in the code names the test it proves
statement: The engine MUST read the product's test files (the files matching the test patterns in the product's configuration, by default the common test and spec file names, never in node_modules, dist or another product's folder, and every file a test record names) and find each test case in them: a call of it or test, with its modifiers and each forms, whose name is a string or template literal, inheriting the names of the describe calls around it. A test case whose name, describes' names and each entries name no ID of a test whose file is the file it is in (or of a product kind's record that proves an obligation) MUST be reported as a test-case-unnamed error naming the file, line and test case.

title: Coverage counts each domain's tests by state
statement: Each domain's coverage MUST report `tests`: how many tests sit in the domain with each state, automated, manual and not automated yet, each test counted once, in the domain its parent belongs to (a pattern rule test in the domain it names). A domain with no tests MUST report zero of each.

title: lathe check reports each domain's tests by state
statement: After a domain's obligation lines, `lathe check`'s coverage report MUST print one line with its tests by state, such as `LA-CHK tests: 50 automated, 0 manual, 7 not automated yet`.

title: The Reader sees each domain's tests by state beside its coverage
statement: The Reader MUST be able to read a product's and each domain's tests by state, automated, manual and not automated yet, beside its coverage, totaled in the product's summary.

title: A domain may follow a pattern and then owes every rule
statement: A `domain` MAY follow a pattern with the `follows` relation. Coverage MUST then count each of the pattern's rules in that domain.

title: A domain follows a pattern itself or through any of its use cases
statement: Coverage and its warnings MUST treat a domain as following a pattern when the domain or any of its use cases follows it (LA-TRC-SP01), and MUST count each rule once there.

title: A product's own kind may be an obligation
statement: A product kind MAY be declared an obligation (`product_kind.obligation`), and coverage MUST then count it as any other obligation kind.

title: A pattern rule is counted for proof alone
statement: For pattern rules, coverage MUST report designed and built as equal to the total and give no design or build gaps, and the `not-designed` and `not-built` warnings MUST NOT fire. Proved, not-automated-yet and proof gaps MUST work as for any obligation.

title: Pattern rules need proof only, and a product cannot widen them
statement: Lathe MUST refuse a product kind that takes the name of one of Lathe's own kinds of record, so a pattern rule asks for proof alone in every domain that owes it.

title: A use case that follows a pattern is not asked for requirements
statement: The `use-case-without-requirements` warning MUST NOT fire for a use case that follows a pattern.

title: Who follows a pattern, and how, can be read
statement: The Owner MUST be able to read which domains and use cases follow a pattern, the patterns a domain or use case follows, and the value one following gives each of the pattern's settings.

title: The Reader reads one requirement's path
statement: On a UC requirement the Reader MUST be able to select it in its use case's line on the Trace stage and read its path: the steps that fulfill it, their technical chain and the tests that prove it, with any gap showing at once.

title: The Trace stage shows the engine's chains and gaps
statement: Each obligation's chain MUST be the engine's, worked out with coverage by the relations it counts: what designs it, what builds it as built counts it, its tests and the files they name. An obligation's gaps MUST be the ones coverage reports, and a flow step, command, query or interface part no obligation's chain reaches MUST be a record-untraced coverage gap, so every interface of Lathe reports the same records. The Trace stage MUST NOT work any of it out itself.

title: The Reader follows each use case from its outcome to its tests
statement: The Reader MUST be able to read each use case of a product once, from the business outcomes its aggregate or read model serves through its requirements, its flow's steps, each interface's version of them and their technical chain to its acceptance tests, with how far each stage has come (designed, built, proved), from the Trace read model.

title: A following ends with its setting values
statement: Stopping the following of a pattern MUST end the domain's or use case's following with the setting values it gave, and the pattern's rules MUST no longer be owed to it.

title: A following that does not exist is refused
statement: Stopping the following of a pattern by one that does not follow it MUST be refused, giving every reason and changing nothing.

title: A fill of a slot ends
statement: Stopping a fill MUST end the technical record's fill of the slot, and coverage MUST no longer count it as debt at the slot.

title: A fill that does not exist is refused
statement: Stopping a fill that does not exist MUST be refused, giving every reason and changing nothing.

title: A record's provider is removed
statement: Removing a provider MUST end the record's being provided from outside the product.

title: A record that has no provider is refused
statement: Removing the provider of a record that has none MUST be refused, giving every reason and changing nothing.

title: The Reader reads coverage for every obligation kind and every test state
statement: The Reader MUST be able to read, for every obligation kind the model names, how much is designed, built and proved, and tell at a glance which tests are automated, manual or not automated yet.

title: The Reader sees which pattern rules a domain owes and whether it proves each
statement: Opening a domain, the Reader MUST see the patterns it follows and, for each rule, whether the domain proves it.

title: The Reader sees what designs, builds and proves an obligation
statement: Opening an obligation, the Reader MUST see below its text what designs it, whether that is built, and the tests under it with their states, each gap called out.

title: A use case shows its requirements designed, built and proved
statement: A use case's Traceability MUST show its requirements with Designed, Built and Proved for each.

title: A technical record shows what it builds and that record's tests
statement: A technical record's Traceability MUST show the obligations it builds and the tests that prove them, each with its state.

title: A test shows what it proves and its run by
statement: A test's Traceability MUST show the obligation it proves and its run by: its level, its state and its file.

title: An operation's file names its method and address
statement: The file of the record that handles an operation MUST name the operation's address, compared in the address normal form (LA-TRC-DS04) and found in code, a string or a comment, with the operation's method written in capitals or called as .post( on the address's line or within two lines of it. Otherwise the engine MUST report an error naming the operation, its method and address, and the file. A record whose file does not exist yet MUST NOT be reported here.

title: A view's address is named in a file of an interface part that renders it
statement: When a view has an address, a file of one of the interface parts that render it MUST name that address, compared in the address normal form (LA-TRC-DS04). Otherwise the engine MUST report an error naming the view, its address and the files it read. A view with no address, or none of whose interface parts' files exists, MUST NOT be reported.

title: Every address the code serves has an operation or a view
statement: The engine MUST read the files of the records that handle the product's operations, and the router files the product's configuration names (glob patterns from the root), for the addresses their code serves: an address literal passed to a method call such as app.get('/tools'), given as a path, pattern or address key or attribute, compared with ===, ==, !== or !=, or assigned to a constant whose name marks it as a path; never one in a comment. A served address that no operation of its method has, and that no view has when it is served for GET or any method, both compared in the address normal form (LA-TRC-DS04), MUST be a coverage gap of the product naming the method, address, file and line.

title: A stored kind's file defines its name, fields and keys
statement: For each entity or read model kept in its own storage that names a file that exists, the engine MUST read that file as text and report a schema-mismatch warning for each part it does not define: the stored kind by its name, each field its entity's or read model's fields give, and each primary, unique and foreign key by its fields, a foreign key also by the stored kind it targets.

title: A stored field's name follows from the field
statement: A field's stored name MUST be the stored name it is given when it gives one, else its name in lower case with every run of other characters an underscore. A field typed by a value object of several fields MUST be flattened into that value object's fields, and an entity's storage MUST also hold the fields of the children kept with its root.

title: A stored kind with no file is a gap
statement: A kind of record kept in its own storage that names no file MUST be reported as a coverage gap.

title: Every package a manifest lists is named by a record
statement: Each package that one of the product's package manifests lists under dependencies, devDependencies, optionalDependencies or peerDependencies MUST be named by a package use of a technical record of the product. Coverage MUST report the packages no record names as one package-not-accounted-for gap on the product, naming each package with the manifests that list it.

title: A record names only a package a manifest lists
statement: A record whose package use names a package that none of its product's package manifests lists MUST be reported by a package-not-in-manifest error naming the record and the package.

title: Only a technical record names a package
statement: Lathe MUST refuse a package use on a record whose kind is not in the technical specification (package-use-technical), Lathe's kinds and a product's own alike, and a package name that is not one npm allows.

title: The manifests are those of the package folders
statement: The manifests MUST be the package manifest of each folder the product's configuration lists as packages, or, when it lists none, of the root and of each folder directly under it (not hidden, not node_modules) that holds one. A listed folder outside the root, or with no package manifest, MUST stop the load with a message naming it.

title: Each record names the outcomes it serves
statement: Each record MUST name the business outcomes it serves, worked out on every read from the use cases whose aggregate or read model serves an outcome, or the aggregate or read model that serves it, or that a step of a journey serving it carries out, and the policies such a journey hands off through, that reach it (LA-TRC-DS06), never stored or typed in: shown on the record as its Serves line, each outcome a link and marked with the journey it is served through, and available through any of Lathe's interfaces as get-serves and list-serves.

title: What no outcome reaches is reported
statement: An aggregate, read model or obligation no outcome reaches MUST be reported by a serves-no-outcome warning that says to write the use case that needs it or remove it, and MUST be listed by list-serves as serving none.

title: A fill of a record that tooling generates is refused
statement: A fill of a record that a tooling record generates MUST be refused, giving every reason and changing nothing: generated records are accounted for already.

title: A fill of a standard or its rule is refused
statement: A fill of a standard or of a standard rule MUST be refused, giving every reason and changing nothing: a standard is the rules that code follows, not code, so an engineering one is accounted for through the records that meet its rules (LA-STD-PRINCIPLES-R06).

title: A record written by hand fills a slot, and coverage counts it as debt
statement: The Owner MUST be able to record that a technical record written by hand fills a slot of a pattern it is owed to, and coverage MUST then list the fill as debt at its slot.

title: A journey's proof is rolled up from its steps and its test
statement: A journey MUST read as proved only when its journey test counts and every step is proved, a use case step when its UC requirements and its flow test are and a handoff when its policy's test is; the roll-up MUST be worked out from the records on every read, never stored, and read the same through any of Lathe's interfaces.

title: A journey's proof shows where its outcomes and use cases are traced
statement: A journey's proof MUST be shown with the journey, with each outcome it serves and in the product's trace between the outcomes and the use cases its steps carry out, and each use case MUST show in its trace the journeys it is a step of.

title: Each journey gap is reported with what to write
statement: A journey without a journey test, with no step on its main path, or serving no outcome, and a step that carries out nothing yet, MUST each be reported as a coverage gap that says what to write.

title: A record has at most one provider
statement: A record MUST have at most one provider; naming another MUST replace the one it had.

title: A change's reach lists every record that depends on it
statement: The reach of a change MUST list every record that names one of the changed records or sits under it, followed on through what designs, builds and proves each, every record once, grouped by stage.

title: The reach names the code and tests a change touches
statement: The reach of a change MUST name each code file that implements a record in it and each test that proves one, with the test's state.

title: The reach names the purposes a change touches
statement: The reach of a change MUST name the use cases, journeys and business outcomes its records serve, so the Owner sees which purposes the change could break.

title: A change of several records reads as one reach
statement: A change of several records MUST be read as one reach, each record in it listed once with the changed records it is reached from, so the Owner can drop a record from the change and see what it no longer touches.

title: An Agent reads the reach the Owner reads
statement: An Agent MUST be able to read the same reach of a change that the Owner reads, before it changes anything.

title: A pattern may have no settings
statement: A pattern MAY have no settings. A rule with no setting MUST apply wherever its pattern is followed, and pattern-setting-missing MUST ask only for the settings a pattern has.

title: Tests start from test data sets
statement: A test data set MUST sit under a domain and MAY give the environment, accounts and starting records some tests need, how to prepare and reset them, and the seed or fixture file that builds them; any kind of test MAY start from any number of them, each a starts_from link.

title: A data set nothing uses, or whose file is missing, is reported
statement: A test data set no test starts from MUST be reported as an error, and one whose file does not exist MUST be reported: as an error when an automated test starts from it, else as a warning.

title: A test data set is found and read whole
statement: The Owner MUST be able to list a domain's test data sets and read one whole, with the tests that start from it, before changing it.

title: Change a test data set refuses what breaks a rule
statement: Changes a test data set's details. It MUST be refused with every reason when what it is given breaks a rule, and leave every data file as it was.

title: Remove a test data set refuses what breaks a rule
statement: Removes a test data set. It MUST be refused with every reason when what it is given breaks a rule, and leave every data file as it was.

title: A test data set moves to another domain
statement: The Owner MUST be able to move a test data set to another domain of its product, where it takes that domain's ID and the tests that start from it name the new ID.

title: Every test gives its run by
statement: Every test MUST give its run by: a level, a state, and a file when it is automated or a manual reason when it is manual. Its file MUST name the test's ID, as LA-TRC-UC05 sets out.

title: A test's state is automated, manual or not automated yet
statement: A test's `state` MUST be one of `automated`, `manual` and `not automated yet`, and every test MUST give one: the store MUST refuse any other value, or none. The checks and coverage MUST read it the same way.

title: Only an automated test needs a file, and only a manual test gives a reason
statement: The store MUST refuse an automated test with no `file`, a manual test with no `manual_reason`, and a manual reason on any other test. A test not automated yet MAY name the file it will live in before that file exists; that MUST be a warning, not an error. Any other file a test names MUST exist (`test-file-missing`, an error).

title: A test's level is one of five
statement: A test's `level` MUST be one of unit, integration, service, system and browser, and the store MUST refuse any other value, or none.

title: A pattern rule is an obligation under a pattern
statement: A pattern rule record MUST sit under a pattern and MUST be an obligation counted for proof alone (LA-TRC-UC07-R05), proved in each domain by a pattern rule test under it that names the domain, at most one per rule and domain. It MAY name, in its setting field, the one pattern setting it depends on.

title: Each domain that follows a pattern owes its rules
statement: Coverage MUST count each pattern rule once in each domain that owes it (LA-TRC-SP04), on that domain's `pattern_rule` line. A domain that does not follow the pattern MUST NOT count the rule, and the rule's gaps MUST name it in each domain that owes it.

title: A domain's own pattern rule test proves a pattern rule there
statement: In each domain that owes a pattern rule, the rule MUST count as proved only when its pattern rule test naming that domain is automated or manual, and as not automated yet when that test is not automated yet. One domain's test MUST NOT count for another.

title: Not-proved warnings name the pattern rule and the domain
statement: The `not-proved` warning MUST report a pattern rule once for each domain that owes it and lacks the proof, with a message naming the rule and the domain, such as "Pattern rule TL-PAT-LIBRARIAN-ACTION-R01 is not proved in TL-LEND", and MUST say when its test there is not automated yet.

title: A pattern that no use case or domain follows is a warning
statement: When no use case and no domain follows a pattern, the engine MUST report a `pattern-not-followed` warning on the pattern, saying how many of its rules are therefore not counted in any domain.

title: An obligation outside every domain counts in Shared
statement: An obligation that sits in no domain, such as a product's own obligation kind declared under the product, MUST count in its product's Shared coverage, so every obligation is counted somewhere. Pattern rules are counted in the domains that owe them (LA-UCS-UC04-R02) and never in Shared.

title: A pattern sits under the product and use cases or domains follow it
statement: A pattern MUST sit under a product and MAY list its settings. A use case, or a domain, MAY follow one or more patterns with the `follows` relation.

title: A pattern is found and read whole
statement: The Owner MUST be able to list a product's patterns and read one whole, with its settings, rules and slots, before changing it.

title: A use case has one flow, whose steps reach operations
statement: The schema MUST have an `interface` under each product, of kind web, API, command line, agent tools, desktop or other, that MAY offer the product's use cases, and at most one `flow` per use case, with `flow_step` under it with a required `position` and `path`; a step MAY fulfill its use case's requirements, invoke a command or query, exchange with integrations and name the one interface it is a variant of.

title: Each use case command changes one use case, held to its rules
statement: Each command of the Use case aggregate MUST load the use case it changes whole through its repository, hold it to the aggregate's rules before it saves, and write only the aggregate's own tables; a refused command MUST give every reason and change no file.

title: Requirements and rules may name a group
statement: A `uc_requirement`, `view_requirement`, `api_requirement`, `pattern_rule` or `standard_rule` MAY name a short heading in `group_name`, such as Validation or Paging, so that a long list of them is sorted under headings as a real product sorts it. A group is a field, not a record, so renaming one MUST change no ID.

title: A use case is found and read whole
statement: The Owner MUST be able to list a domain's use cases by group and read one whole, with its requirements, flow and tests, before changing it.

title: A use case sits in one domain, and its ID names it
statement: A use case MUST name the domain it sits in, and its ID MUST start with that domain's ID.

title: A pattern rule is owed by every domain that follows it, and proved per domain
statement: A pattern rule MUST be an obligation of each domain that follows its pattern, or has a use case that does, proved by one pattern rule test per rule and domain.

title: Change a pattern rule refuses what breaks a rule
statement: Changes a pattern rule's title, statement, group or notes. It MUST be refused with every reason when what it is given breaks a rule, and leave every data file as it was.

title: A flow's ID is its use case's and FL
statement: A flow's ID MUST be its use case's ID and FL (TL-LEND-UC01-FL); `next-id` MUST give it, and refuse a use case that already has its flow.

title: An interface that offers no use case is a gap
statement: An interface that offers no use case MUST be reported as a gap (interface-offers-nothing).

title: A use case with no flow is a coverage gap, never an error
statement: A use case with no flow MUST be reported in its domain's coverage as a `use-case-without-flow` gap, a record short of a minimum. It MUST NOT be an error, so `lathe check` does not fail because of it.

title: A requirement a flow misses is a gap
statement: A UC requirement that no step of its use case's flow fulfills MUST be reported as not designed, naming the flow.

title: Every interface that offers a use case reaches its steps
statement: A step that invokes a command or query MUST be reached by every interface that offers its use case, but for another interface's variant and a step that exchanges with an integration that performs its use case: an app a person works in by a view that presents it, calls other programs make by the call that exposes it, a command line or agent tools by a record of the product's own interface design kinds under it or that presents it (one that sits under an interface for that interface only, any other for every command line and agent tools of the product, as a view of every such interface or of one); one that is not MUST be warned of (step-unreached). A variant of an interface that does not offer its use case MUST be an error (variant-not-offered); a flow no interface offers and no integration performs, and an interface that offers a use case none of whose actors it lists among its roles, MUST be warned of (flow-not-offered, interface-actor-not-the-use-case).

title: A path whose positions skip a number is a step-order error
statement: The steps on each path of a flow SHOULD run 1, 2, 3 without a gap, the path compared trimmed and in any letter case. A path whose positions skip a number MUST be reported once as a `step-order` error, on the first step after the gap.

title: A step is written once, whatever the interface
statement: Variant steps of one flow on two or more interfaces that invoke the same command or query MUST be an error (step-repeated-per-interface): a step says what the actor does or learns, and each interface's version says how.

title: A use case can be changed
statement: The Owner or an Agent MUST be able to change a use case's title, goal, result or notes, or its actors (the whole list, in order), and its domain MUST change only by Move a use case.

title: A UC requirement can be added
statement: The Owner or an Agent MUST be able to add a UC requirement to its use case.

title: A UC requirement can be changed
statement: The Owner or an Agent MUST be able to change a UC requirement's title, statement or group (a rule of a use case).

title: A UC requirement can be removed
statement: The Owner or an Agent MUST be able to remove a UC requirement with its use case tests and the links they start (a rule of a use case), and it MUST be refused while a step fulfills it, or anything else references it or its tests.

title: A flow can be changed
statement: The Owner or an Agent MUST be able to change a flow's title, which is its use case's.

title: A flow step can be changed
statement: The Owner or an Agent MUST be able to change a step's title or the interface it is a variant of (null makes it every interface's), or its links: a list given replaces the list, null clears what it invokes, and its path and position MUST change only by Move a flow step.

title: A flow step can be removed
statement: The Owner or an Agent MUST be able to remove a flow step with the links it starts (one step of a flow), and it MUST be refused while anything else references it.

title: A use case test can be removed
statement: The Owner or an Agent MUST be able to remove a use case test with the links it starts (a test of one requirement), and it MUST be refused while anything else references it, such as a business outcome it measures.

title: A flow test can be changed
statement: The Owner or an Agent MUST be able to change a flow test's way of running or the test data sets it starts from (the whole list) (a test of a whole flow's main path).

title: Each interface's version of a flow is derived, never stored
statement: Each interface that offers a use case MUST have its own version of the use case's flow, worked out from the steps and never stored: its actor (the first of the use case's actors it lists), the patterns it follows and their rules, and its steps without the other interfaces' variants, each with where it is carried out.

title: A flow test can be removed
statement: The Owner or an Agent MUST be able to remove a flow test with the links it starts (a test of a whole flow's main path), and it MUST be refused while anything else references it, such as a business outcome it measures.

title: A pattern can be changed
statement: The Owner or an Agent MUST be able to change a pattern's title, description or notes, or its settings (the whole list, in order), and its product MUST NOT change.

title: A pattern can be removed
statement: The Owner or an Agent MUST be able to remove a pattern whole: its settings, rules and rule tests, and the links they start, and it MUST be refused while anything outside it references what is in it, such as a follower.

title: A pattern rule can be removed
statement: The Owner or an Agent MUST be able to remove a pattern rule with its tests and the links they start, and it MUST be refused while anything references it or them.

title: A pattern rule test can be changed
statement: The Owner or an Agent MUST be able to change a pattern rule test's way of running, the domain it proves the rule in, or the test data sets it starts from (the whole list).

title: A pattern rule test can be removed
statement: The Owner or an Agent MUST be able to remove a pattern rule test and the links it starts, and it MUST be refused while anything references it.

title: A slot can be added
statement: The Owner or an Agent MUST be able to add a slot to its pattern: an open-ended part code fills against its contract, with the reason its fills vary by design when they do.

title: A slot can be changed
statement: The Owner or an Agent MUST be able to change a slot's title or contract, or the reason its fills vary by design; null clears the reason, and its pattern MUST NOT change.

title: A slot can be removed
statement: The Owner or an Agent MUST be able to remove a slot from its pattern, and it MUST be refused while a record fills it.

title: A flow step can be moved
statement: The Owner or an Agent MUST be able to move a step to another position, on its own path or another, shifting the steps of the old path and the new so each stays numbered 1, 2, 3.

title: A record of a use case goes with what it holds, refused while referenced
statement: Removing a use case, or a requirement, flow, step or test in one, MUST take what sits under it and the links they start, and MUST be refused, naming what does, while anything left still references them.

title: A use case belongs to its result's domain
statement: A use case, and everything under it, MUST belong to its domain, which is its result's, so that its obligations count in that domain's coverage exactly as they did directly under the domain. A use case moved to another domain, with a result there, takes that domain's IDs.

title: A moved use case takes the new domain's IDs
statement: A record moved to another domain of its product MUST take that domain's ID in place of the old one's, with everything under it, and every record that names one of them MUST name the new ID; a use case whose new ID another use case of that domain already has MUST take the next free number there; a domain of another product MUST be refused.

title: A requirement moved to another use case takes that use case's next number
statement: Moving a UC requirement to another use case of its product MUST give it the next free number under that use case, and its tests the new requirement's ID in place of the old one's, and MUST carry each new ID into every record that names the old one. A requirement a step of its own use case still fulfills MUST be refused until the step no longer does.

title: A test gives its size and markers
statement: A test's run by MAY give its size, volume or worst case, and is small when it gives none; it MAY mark itself smoke or external, each only as yes, and the store MUST refuse small and a marker of no, which are written by leaving them out.

title: A test changed to automated names its file
statement: A test changed to automated MUST name the file that runs it.

title: What a step carries out cannot be removed under it
statement: Removing a use case or policy a journey step carries out MUST be refused, naming the step, until the step is removed or linked to another; removing a journey MUST remove its steps and its test, never what they carry out.
